body:
I persevered with the Sinclair Method protocol (taking one pill an hour before drinking to dull the effects of alcohol, thus causing extinction of the addiction over time) as I was persuaded by my research and high hopes of successfully reducing my drinking using this method.
After 3 months, I became more physically dependent on alcohol than I'd ever been in my life, had extreme depression, ongoing menstrual bleeding which is unusual at my age, a very red face, low energy, etc.
The rebound anxiety caused me to drink even more and perhaps because I wasn't getting the drunk feeling immediately I would drink larger amounts more quickly and have very bad cravings, contrary what the literature said should happen. Can't really explain why but it was not a good drug for me.
